newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian school bans "graphic" passion play.
newsitem.headline: Australian school bans "graphic" passion play.

text.p: An Australian school has created a biblical furore by banning the traditional Easter passion play portraying the trial and crucifixion of Jesus Christ for being too violent.

Monteagle Public School in rural New South Wales state suspended performances of the play after its principal decided graphic depictions of Christ's death breached government anti-violence guidelines for schools.
The play performed at the school in March included scenes where the 12-year-old child playing Christ carried a heavy cross and had his clothes torn off to reveal fake blood.

Officials backed the school's move. "We have children from kindergarten to year six witnessing very graphic scenes of whipping, shouting, humiliation, spitting and ridicule," state education minister John Aquilina told parliament.
But church leaders disagreed. The New South Wales council of churches said on Thursday the ban was a "total absurdity".
